description.p: A native replacement for GamaKay's Windows app: lighting, keymaps and macros for the LK67, written straight to the keyboard's onboard memory over USB.
Nothing stays resident — every command writes to the keyboard and exits — and the keyboard keeps typing while it is configured, because the kernel's HID driver stays bound.

ul.li: Lighting modes, brightness, speed and colour, with a live preview
Remap keys on the base and Fn layers, across the board's 8 profiles
A macro recorder, and a scriptable command line tool

description.p: The underglow's colour now applies: with the rainbow bit stored the board shows its own palette and ignores the colour, so a colour write clears it. The Underglow panel gains a Rainbow toggle to ask for the palette explicitly.
The board's underglow works: its side and bottom-mesh LEDs get their own panel, with modes and a colour wheel of their own. GamaKay's software leaves these LEDs alone.
The window now announces its application id, so a desktop shell associates the running app with its launcher entry and shows its icon instead of a generic one.
First release: lighting, keymaps, macros, the GUI and CLI, and packages for Arch, Debian/Ubuntu, Fedora/RHEL and AppImage.
